points.description: States that the algorithm finds/selects the minimum (smallest) element among the remaining elements, i.e. the part of the array not yet processed.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if the answer mentions finding the smallest/minimum element but does not make clear that it is selected from the remaining/unsorted elements.

levels.says: Mentions finding the smallest/minimum element but does not specify that it is chosen from the remaining elements.

points.description: States that the selected minimum is swapped with the current element (the element at the current position).
points.partial_credit: Half credit if the answer mentions swapping or placing the minimum into position but does not say it is swapped with the current element.

levels.says: Mentions swapping or placing the minimum into its position but does not clearly say it is swapped with the current element.

points.description: States that the array is processed one element at a time, moving from left to right (or from the start toward the end).
points.partial_credit: Half credit if the answer mentions processing elements one at a time or scanning the array but does not give the left-to-right/start-to-end order.

levels.says: Mentions processing elements one at a time or scanning the array but not the left-to-right/start-to-end order.

rubric.notes: Full marks require all three ideas: selecting the minimum from the remaining elements, swapping it with the current element, and proceeding one element at a time from left to right. Part marks are given when one of these ideas is present but vague or missing a key detail. No marks are earned for merely naming selection sort or giving an unrelated sorting description.
